correctness.rationale: On exactly two scalar quadratics with positive unequal curvatures and distinct minimizers, each component proximal map is an affine contraction. Each two-component epoch has common multiplier r=(1+ha)^(-1)(1+hb)^(-1) in (0,1); its two random offsets differ by h^2 ab(u-v)r. The IID Bernoulli offset recurrence gives the stationary mean and variance and exact risk in RESULT.md, with no unproved convergence assumption. Differentiating risk gives strictly positive curvature 4r Delta^2/((1-r)^2(1+r)), and constrained minimization yields the stated clipped p_star and unique threshold. Taylor expansion gives the two displayed distinct h^2 and h^3 constants; direct rational verifier (verify.py) passed 15624 assertions with recorded output. Finite tests validate arithmetic rather than infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Changing the permutation law leaves the exact same two proximal component calls per epoch and same strongly convex finite-sum objective. The result sharply classifies every admissible Bernoulli order law, finds the unique unbiased law, and identifies an unexpected interior-to-deterministic risk-optimal phase transition as step size increases. The h^2 versus h^3 stationary squared-error difference supplies genuine numerical-design consequence in a canonical non-interpolating model. This is a complete analytically motivated benchmark, not a renamed textbook limit or arbitrary parameter slice; no higher-dimensional universality is asserted.
